result.topic_en: Euler sets up Case II of his theory of fluid friction: water flowing from a large upper vessel through a vertical pipe made of two cylindrical parts, and gives the formula for the height corresponding to the efflux velocity.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 363

CASVS II.

SI AQVA EX VASE SVPREMO PER TVBVM
VERTICALEM EX DVABVS PARTIBVS
CYLINDRICIS COMPOSITVM
EFFLVIT.

67. Sit vasis supremi amplitudo AA $=ff$, quae fit valde magna, eiusque altitudo AB $=a$, quod vas iugiter aqua plenum conseruari pono. Ex hoc vase aqua primum in tubum BC fluat, cuius amplitudo sit BB $=gg$ et altitudo BC $=b$: cui tubo in CC annexus sit insuper tubus verticalis CD, amplitudinis $=hh$ et longitudinis CD $=c$: cuius basis infima pertusa sit foramine DD $=kk$, per quod aqua in aerem effluat. Significet autem $l$ altitudinem columnae aqueae atmosphaerae aequiponderantem: sit autem $kk$ prae $ff$ tam paruum, vt valor $\mathfrak{f}=\frac{k^4}{f^4}$ pro nihilo haberi possit.

Tab. VII. Fig. 2.

68. His positis sit breuitatis gratia $\mathfrak{A}=e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{f}}$; $A=\frac{1-\mathfrak{A}}{\alpha}$; $\mathfrak{B}=e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{g}}$; $B=\frac{1-\mathfrak{B}}{\alpha}$; $\mathfrak{C}=e^{\frac{-\alpha c}{h}}$; $C=\frac{1-\mathfrak{C}}{\alpha}$, tum vero $\mathfrak{g}=\frac{k^4}{g^4}$ et $\mathfrak{h}=\frac{k^4}{h^4}$. Iam aqua per orificium DD $=kk$ effluere inuenta est celeritate debita altitudini $v$, vt sit
$$v=\frac{A\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C}f+B\mathfrak{C}g+Ch-(1-\mathfrak{A}\mathfrak{B}\mathfrak{C})l}{1-(1-\mathfrak{B})\mathfrak{C}\mathfrak{g}-(1-\mathfrak{C})\mathfrak{h}}$$
vnde, vt iam supra notauimus, sequitur, si frictio euanesceret, fore $v=a+b+c$, ita vt altitudo celeritati effluxus debita esset aequalis toti altitudini AD.

69. Si amplitudo tubi medii BC aequalis esset amplitudini infimi CD, casus ad praecedentem rediret;
Zz 2 sin

items.quote: Iam aqua per orificium DD $=kk$ effluere inuenta est celeritate debita altitudini $v$, vt sit
items.english: Now the water has been found to flow out through the orifice DD = kk with the velocity due to the height v, so that v equals the given expression.

items.quote: si frictio euanesceret, fore $v=a+b+c$, ita vt altitudo celeritati effluxus debita esset aequalis toti altitudini AD.
items.english: If friction vanished, v = a + b + c, so that the height due to the efflux velocity would equal the total height AD.

items.quote: Si amplitudo tubi medii BC aequalis esset amplitudini infimi CD, casus ad praecedentem rediret;
items.english: If the cross-section of the middle tube BC were equal to that of the lowest tube CD, the case would reduce to the preceding one.
